dither

/DITH-er/ - rhymes with wither · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Dither means to be indecisive.

Standing at the trailhead map, the hikers dithered between the ridge loop and the falls path until the morning fog burned off.

Example

The gallery owner dithered over the invitation list for weeks — adding a name each morning, striking two each night — until the printer's deadline passed and the opening went unannounced.

Dither is more damning than 'hesitate': hesitation is a pause before acting, while dithering is fussy, drawn-out indecision that never quite becomes a decision at all.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

waver: To waver is to falter briefly in your resolve — a moment's wobble before you steady yourself and go on. Dither is longer and fussier: wavering passes, while dithering is drawn-out indecision that keeps circling the choice without ever landing on it.

stall: To stall is to delay on purpose, buying time — the person stalling has already decided what they want and is playing for position. Dither is the opposite failure: a ditherer delays because they genuinely cannot decide, fussing at the choice with no tactic behind it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

decide: to land on a choice

commit: to bind yourself to a course and stay

Where it sits · how completely doubt stalls movement

hesitate → dither → freeze

hesitate vs. dither: To hesitate is milder than to dither — a single beat of doubt before you move.

freeze vs. dither: Freeze goes further than dither: the fussing stops and nothing moves at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — dither: to tremble, to quiver (Middle English didderen)

Put it together: Dither is a single root with nothing to detach — a Middle English shiver-word whose trembling turned mental: a mind quivering between options without ever moving.

Why there's no relative to spot: Dither comes from Middle English didderen, 'to tremble or shake' — a stand-alone shiver word. The mental back-and-forth sense grew from that image of quivering in place, and nothing else in English descends from it.

Strength Check

Word Choice

informal, mildly mocking

Dither is the everyday, slightly teasing word for fussing over a choice without landing anywhere. Its unit-mate vacillate is its formal cousin and swings between definite positions; dithering never even gets that far.
